title: Navigation API: Specify and test `state` persistence across tab discards, crashes, and session restore

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#2 — filed by @domenic (2021-02), originally from `slightlyoff/history_api#17` by @jakearchibald.

---

The intent is that `NavigationHistoryEntry`'s state behaves the same as `history.state` in terms of persistence under:

- tab discard (common on mobile)
- tab crashes
- browser restarts that restore the session

The original issue's point was that **we don't actually know what `history.state` does in these scenarios**, and it isn't specified or tested. Since the navigation API is defined in terms of the same session history infrastructure, that gap now sits under both APIs.

This is a spec-and-test gap in HTML proper rather than a feature request, which is why it's being migrated rather than dropped. Testing is admittedly awkward (likely manual; crashes possibly via OOM), but the specified behaviour could at least be pinned down.

Original issue asked @natechapin about Chrome's behaviour; that was never answered.
